meeting_header:
Date: 2025-08-20
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Head of ML - NexusHealth), Daniel Lee (Platform Eng), Alicia Gomez (CTO)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood POC against customer's baseline provider. Discussed p50/p95 latency, throughput, tuning opportunities (quantization, batching, KV cache), cost tradeoffs, security concerns (VPC, SOC2, KMS), and next steps for additional tuning and data sharing.
topics: Benchmark numbers: p50/p95/p99 latencies and throughput vs baseline
Tuning: quantization (int8), KV cache warmup, batching policies
Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
Security/compliance: SOC2 scope, KMS, audit logs
Next steps and action items: spreadsheet, raw logs, traffic sample
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya Sharma: Priya here.
[00:07] Daniel Lee: Daniel on the call.
[00:09] Alicia Gomez: Alicia here.
[00:10] Marco Diaz: Marco here from Redwood.
[00:12] Sofia Patel: Great, cool. Today's agenda is benchmark review vs your current baseline provider and then talk through tuning items and next steps. Marco, you want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:22] Marco Diaz: Yeah, sure. So first slide, um, quick note on methodology, we ran identical prompt sets you shared — about 12k requests representing mix of short and long sequences, we ran three runs per config, we measured p50/p95/p99 latencies and steady-state throughput. We tried to replicate baseline concurrency; there may be small diffs in batch sizes.
[00:40] Marco Diaz: Baseline (AltModelCo) numbers: p50 ~120 ms, p95 ~420 ms, p99 ~820 ms, throughput ~360 req/s on their managed vCPU+GPU instance we could see. Cost estimate from their billing data you shared is roughly $0.27 per 1k tokens when factoring their autoscaling.
[00:58] Marco Diaz: Redwood hosted (default quant, batching auto): p50 ~85 ms, p95 ~270 ms, p99 ~560 ms, throughput ~520 req/s, estimated cost $0.20 per 1k tokens. Note these are from our standard hosted profile, no int8 applied.
[01:15] Priya Sharma: Okay, that p95 delta is interesting — 420 down to 270 — is that across all sequence lengths or skewed to longer ones?
[01:21] Marco Diaz: Good question. It's skewed — for short prompts (<128 tokens) p95 is closer to 180 ms, for long prompts (512–1024) it tails up. Our p95 numbers I quoted are aggregate across the mix. We can break it down.
[01:33] Daniel Lee: There's also throughput— you said 520 req/s versus 360, that's a big difference. Did you use KV cache in those runs?
[01:38] Marco Diaz: The initial runs used prefix caching for repeated prompts but not an aggressive warmup. We have a separate run that enables heavy KV cache warmup and that pushes effective throughput to ~640 req/s and lowers long-tail latency — p95 drops another ~40–60 ms on long sequences.
[01:51] Alicia Gomez: Are you sure the baseline is configured optimally? I know AltModelCo has a number of knobs.
[01:56] Sofia Patel: We tried to match their recommended settings, but we did rely on the logs Nexus gave us; there could be config differences. That's why Daniel's permission to look at their perf logs would help.
[02:06] Priya Sharma: We can share more of the baseline logs, yeah.
[02:09] Daniel Lee: We'll try to pull a sanitized export. No guarantees on how much we can share but we'll try.
[02:14] Marco Diaz: Awesome. A few more items — tuning: we tested int8 quantization on a dedicated Redwood profile (same model weights) and saw CPU/GPU utilization drop and cost estimate down ~18%, with p50 roughly constant and p95 increase small for the worst-case long sequences — p95 went from 270 to ~300 ms in the aggregate run, but the throughput improved to ~700 req/s.
[02:36] Priya Sharma: Wait so quantization improved throughput but slightly worsened p95? Is that consistent?
[02:40] Marco Diaz: Yeah that's the tradeoff we often see. Quantization reduces compute time for many tokens but can increase tail latency in certain kernels for long sequences, depending on kernel selection and memory layout. We have a hybrid approach we can try — int8 for shorter sequences, fp16 for long ones — that gives the best of both worlds.
[02:56] Alicia Gomez: What's the risk to output quality with int8? We run clinical summarization, small hallucination changes could be a problem.
[03:02] Marco Diaz: Absolutely, quality check is required. Our Redwood Optimize evals run your prompt set and will score rouge/semantic similarity against your baseline. So far on your eval subset the delta was negligible for int8 — like <0.7% on our similarity metric — but we flagged a handful of edge cases. We can run a targeted eval on the 150 critical prompts you flagged.
[03:22] Priya Sharma: Good, let's do that.
[03:24] Sofia Patel: Security question came up last week — VPC/private deployment scope. Alicia, you mentioned you needed SOC2 and KMS for keys?
[03:31] Alicia Gomez: Right. SOC2 is a hard req, we need audit trail, SSO, KMS integration and the ability to keep logs in our project. Also interested in dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[03:41] Marco Diaz: Redwood Private (VPC) supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs — we can hand over an architecture diagram. For dedicated pools we can provision reserved capacity as well; that reduces tail variance and gives predictable throughput.
[03:51] Daniel Lee: Any latency delta for private compared to hosted? I assume network egress might add a few ms.
[03:55] Marco Diaz: Correct — if you run in your VPC with our runtime in your region, network overhead is typically 5–12 ms median extra, depending on colocated infra. But the tradeoff is lower tail variance due to reserved GPUs and no multi-tenant interference.
[04:08] Priya Sharma: For SLA, our internal target p95 under production mix is 300 ms or lower. Does Redwood hit that with dedicated?
[04:14] Marco Diaz: Yes, with dedicated pool + aggressive KV-cache and hybrid quant plan we expect aggregate p95 around 230–280 ms for your mix. We'll validate in the next run.
[04:22] Sofia Patel: Great. Back to the bench numbers — Marco, can you quickly run through the run-to-run variance and CI?
[04:27] Marco Diaz: Sure. Across three runs, p95 standard deviation was about 12–18 ms for Redwood hosted, baseline had higher variance ~25–40 ms. The int8 runs had slightly higher variance on long tails. We can include full run CSVs in the shared sheet.
[04:41] Priya Sharma: You mentioned cost numbers earlier — can you share cost per 1M tokens for both?
[04:45] Marco Diaz: Baseline ~ $270 per 1M tokens (est) — remember that includes their autoscale inefficiencies. Redwood hosted ~ $200 per 1M tokens with default config; int8/dedicated can drop estimate to ~$165 per 1M tokens depending on your run rate. Those are ballpark, we'll do a precise cost modeling worksheet.
[05:02] Daniel Lee: On the cost modeling — does that include request-level overhead like network, logs storage, and model variant fallbacks?
[05:08] Marco Diaz: Good call — the model numbers are compute+infra. We suggested adding a 7–12% overhead for logs + network + storage depending on retention. For fallbacks when you run multi-variant rollouts, additional cost applies but we can set automated fallback policies to minimize double-spend.
[05:22] Alicia Gomez: Any concerns about degradation during peak? We have daily spikes.
[05:26] Marco Diaz: Autoscaling + reserved burst capacity can handle spikes. For strict SLOs we recommend dedicated with headroom or a hybrid reserved+burst plan — that removes risk of transient tails from noisy neighbors.
[05:36] Priya Sharma: One thing — our legal/privacy team needs clarification on data retention for hosted logs. Can you provide retention options and encryption-at-rest details?
[05:44] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll include a security brief. Short answer: hosted has configurable retention windows, data immutability, encryption-at-rest with customer KMS on Private. We'll attach SOC2 certs and the KMS integration doc.
[05:55] Daniel Lee: Awesome. For the next run, what do you need from us to validate the dedicated plan?
[05:59] Marco Diaz: Two things: (1) a 2-hour production traffic sample we can replay (anonymized), and (2) permission to run the heavy KV-cache warmup on a dedicated pool. That will let us measure realistic steady-state.
[06:11] Priya Sharma: We'll prepare the sample, anonymize it, and aim to share by Friday.
[06:15] Sofia Patel: Perfect. Any other questions?
[06:17] Alicia Gomez: One quick question on observability — will we get per-route token breakdown and tracing?
[06:22] Marco Diaz: Yes Redwood Console exposes per-route token cost, p50/p95, tracing, and error analysis. We can give you a demo account with sample dashboards.
[06:30] Priya Sharma: We'll want RBAC to limit engineer access to logs.
[06:33] Marco Diaz: Supported — RBAC + SSO.
[06:35] Sofia Patel: Okay let's recap next steps — Sofia will share spreadsheets and security docs, Marco will run tuned int8+hybrid runs and KV warmup, Priya will provide sample traffic and success criteria, Daniel will try to export baseline logs. We'll sync next Tuesday same time. Any objections?
[06:51] Daniel Lee: Works for me.
[06:52] Priya Sharma: Works.
[06:53] Alicia Gomez: Fine.
[06:54] Sofia Patel: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email and links.
[06:58] Marco Diaz: Thanks all.
[07:00] [meeting end]

Notes: Some transcription words may be slightly off (e.g., "KV cahce" typo flagged in raw ASR).
